reason: Prioritize transpose-focused tests: vector_access and a_transpose target the packing cost while preserving the consumer, and tail_alignment is a smaller change with limited correctness scope. Cache-stride and alignment tests follow because their benefit is speculative and they affect the full transpose and consumption path. Scheduling and loop changes rank lower because supplied pointer and compiler experiments had inconclusive paired results; the K-unroll proposals are unverified and may raise register pressure. Panel packing adds timed work, and the B-panel proposal also adds a full packing pass. The earlier transpose-plus-GEMM fusion and B-packing trials regressed sharply, but those joint results do not establish causality.
